4500.name: The Garden

north.description: To the north lies The Garden.

east.description: To the east lies The Garden.

south.description: To the south lies The Great Field Of Garathorm.

west.description: To the west lies By The Pond.

4500.description:
You step through a gap in the old garden wall, with the trade road
behind you to the south, running back across the Great Field of
Garathorm. The gravel path is split by shoots of knotweed and lined with
flowers far too bright, red as fresh wounds and violet as bruises. The
air is warm, heavy and sweet. Paths lead on north and east between the
beds, and west toward the glint of a pond.

4501.name: The Garden

north.description: To the north lies By The Pond.

east.description: To the east lies The Garden.

south.description: To the south lies The Garden.

4501.description:
Rose bushes the size of haystacks have swallowed this part of the
garden, their thorns hooked and their blooms wet with a sticky dew. The
path narrows to a single trampled line between them. It runs north
toward the edge of a pond, east along more overgrown beds, and south
back to the garden's entrance. Something rustles among the roses and
then goes still.

4502.name: The Garden

north.description: To the north lies The Path Around The Greenhouse.

east.description: To the east lies The Field Of Crab Grass.

south.description: To the south lies The Garden.

west.description: To the west lies The Garden.

4502.description:
Four paths cross here amid overgrown flowerbeds, and a toppled stone urn
lies in a drift of nettles. Giant sunflowers lean over the way, their
dark faces turned to follow you. From this crossing the way leads north
toward the glasshouse, west to the rose-choked beds, south to more
garden, and east into a patch of wiry grass.

4503.name: By The Pond

north.description: To the north lies On The Small Island.

east.description: To the east lies The Garden.

west.description: To the west lies On The Winding Path.

4503.description:
The pond stretches out beside the path here, wide and brown, with a
small island rising from its centre. Stepping stones, green with slime,
make a crooked line through the shallows to the north. A willow trails
its branches in the water, and the bank is churned by heavy, dragging
marks. The path leads east to the garden's entrance and west along a
winding way.

4504.name: By The Pond

north.description: To the north lies Outside The Greenhouse.

south.description: To the south lies The Garden.

4504.description:
A round pond lies here, its surface so choked with lily pads and green
scum that the water is almost invisible. Dragonflies as long as a hand
hover and dart above it, and the reeds along the bank sway though no
wind stirs. The path bends away north toward a great glasshouse, and
south it returns to the tangled garden. The mud at the water's edge is
printed with narrow, dragging marks.

4505.name: The Garden

north.description: To the north lies The Garden.

west.description: To the west lies The Garden.

4505.description:
This corner of the garden was once a kitchen plot, and the ghosts of
cabbages and onions still sprawl in the beds, grown to a monstrous size.
A rotting scarecrow's post stands among them, its crossbar empty.
Lettuce leaves as broad as shields tremble beside the path. The way runs
north toward a crossing of paths, and west to the garden's entrance.

4506.name: The Field Of Crab Grass

west.description: To the west lies The Garden.

4506.description:
A thick mat of crab grass has overrun the old lawn, its jointed stems
creeping out in all directions and rooting at every node. The grass hums
with a faint dry clicking, like claws on glass. A low wall of crumbling
brick closes the field in, and a rusted croquet hoop leans in the
tangle. The only path out leads west back to the garden.

4507.name: Outside The Greenhouse

north.description: To the north lies In The Greenhouse.

east.description: To the east lies The Path Around The Greenhouse.

south.description: To the south lies By The Pond.

4507.description:
The greenhouse rises before you, a long hall of iron ribs and clouded
glass, many panes cracked and furred with green. Its door hangs open on
a single hinge, and warm wet air breathes out of it, thick with the
smell of rot and honey. The path leads north through the doorway into
the glasshouse, east along its outer wall, and south back to the pond.
Pale tendrils have crept out through the broken panes and curl over the
frame.

4508.name: On The Small Island

north.description: To the north lies By The Pond.

south.description: To the south lies By The Pond.

4508.description:
The island is a small hump of black earth, crowned with one gnarled tree
whose branches are hung with strings of pale, glistening seed pods.
Reeds ring the shore, and the water laps at the roots in slow oily
swells. A cracked statue of a stooped man lies half sunk in the mud.
Stepping stones lead south to the near bank and north across the water
to the far one.

4509.name: On The Winding Path

east.description: To the east lies By The Pond.

west.description: To the west lies Outside The Greenhouse.

4509.description:
The path winds between hedges of box that have run wild, its gravel
hidden under creeping moss. Passion flowers, bright as painted fans,
hang from the branches in garlands. The ground squelches underfoot, and
the scent of damp bark is strong. East the way runs back to the pond,
and west it brings you to the foot of the glasshouse.

4510.name: The Path Around The Greenhouse

north.description: To the north lies The Path Around The Greenhouse.

south.description: To the south lies The Path Around The Greenhouse.

west.description: To the west lies In The Greenhouse.

4510.description:
A flagged path hugs the outer wall of the glasshouse, its stones heaved
up by roots and fringed with pale moss. Condensation runs down the glass
in long streaks, and shapes shift behind it in the green light. The path
runs north and south along the wall, and a glass door to the west leads
back into the greenhouse. A trellis of dead vines leans against the
frame, its blossoms crumbling to brown dust.

4511.name: The Path Around The Greenhouse

north.description: To the north lies The Clearing.

south.description: To the south lies The Path Around The Greenhouse.

4511.description:
The path follows the glasshouse into a quieter, shadier stretch, where
the glass is so stained with algae that the greenhouse shows only as a
dark bulk. Foxgloves taller than a man crowd both sides, their speckled
bells nodding together. A rusting watering can lies on its side at the
verge. North the path opens onto bare ground, and south it follows the
wall back around.

4512.name: The Path Around The Greenhouse

north.description: To the north lies The Path Around The Greenhouse.

south.description: To the south lies The Garden.

west.description: To the west lies Outside The Greenhouse.

4512.description:
The path swings round the corner of the glasshouse here, where the iron
frame has rusted to the colour of dried blood. A rain barrel stands
under a downpipe, brimming over with green water. Hyacinths and lilies
crowd the verges in a heavy, sickly perfume. The path runs north along
the wall, south to a garden of tangled beds, and west toward the
greenhouse door.

4513.name: The Plaza

east.description: To the east lies The Plaza.

south.description: To the south lies The Hedge Labyrinth.

4513.description:
This end of the plaza is overlooked by a tall wall of clipped yew, its
face trimmed flat and dark as a cliff. Cracked tiles form a mosaic of a
spreading flower, half of it hidden under creeping weeds. The plaza
continues east, and a narrow gap in the hedge leads south into the
labyrinth. A cold draught seeps out of that gap, smelling of earth and
old leaves.

4515.name: The Plaza

north.description: To the north lies The Pavilion.

south.description: To the south lies The Clearing.

west.description: To the west lies The Plaza.

4515.description:
A paved plaza spreads out here, its flagstones cracked and lifted by
weeds with pink flowers that glisten like raw meat. A dry fountain in
the centre holds a stone nymph whose face has been eaten smooth by moss.
Curved iron benches face a white pavilion, which stands to the north,
while the clearing lies south and another stretch of the plaza west.
Humidity beads on every surface.

extra_descs.fountain nymph statue:
The stone nymph holds an empty urn above a basin of dry leaves. Moss has
crept over her features, so that she seems to wear a green mask.

4516.name: The Clearing

north.description: To the north lies The Plaza.

east.description: To the east lies The Rockery.

south.description: To the south lies The Path Around The Greenhouse.

4516.description:
A round clearing opens in the garden, its grass flattened as though by
some great weight. A sundial stands in the middle, its bronze gnomon
bent and its face blotched with lichen. Paving shows through the weeds
to the north, where a plaza begins, and a heap of grey rock rises to the
east. The path back along the glasshouse leads south.

extra_descs.sundial gnomon:
The bronze gnomon is bent far out of true, and the hours around the dial
are overgrown with lichen. Someone has scratched the words 'Nothing
keeps time here' into the rim.

4517.name: The Hedge Labyrinth

north.description: To the north lies The Plaza.

south.description: To the south lies The Hedge Labyrinth.

4517.description:
Walls of dense, thorny hedge rise on every side, twice the height of a
man and woven so tight that no light slips between the leaves. The
gravel underfoot is dark and damp, strewn with snapped twigs. Branches
stir softly in the corridors though the air is still. The only open way
is the gap to the north, leading back to the plaza.

4518.name: The Hedge Labyrinth

north.description: To the north lies The Hedge Labyrinth.

south.description: To the south lies The Hedge Labyrinth.

4518.description:
Another passage between the high hedges, this one narrow enough that
thorns catch at your sleeves on either side. The gravel is slick with a
black ooze, and a trail of crushed leaves winds on and bends out of
sight. Somewhere deeper in, the hedge creaks as though it were
stretching.

4519.name: The Hedge Labyrinth

north.description: To the north lies The Hedge Labyrinth.

south.description: To the south lies The Hedge Labyrinth.

4519.description:
A small square in the maze, with a rotted wooden seat set into a niche
cut in the hedge. The leaves overhead are woven so densely they make a
green ceiling, and a damp gloom lies over everything. Tiny white flowers
grow in the seat's cracks, sweet and sickly. Every gap leads into yet
another wall of green.

4520.name: The Hedge Labyrinth

north.description: To the north lies The Hedge Labyrinth.

south.description: To the south lies The Hedge Labyrinth.

4520.description:
The hedges here have been clipped into the shapes of animals: a stag, a
hound, a swan, each now overgrown into a shaggy parody. Moisture
glitters on the leaves, and the gravel crunches loudly in the hush. A
smell of crushed mint and something meatier hangs in the air. The
topiary seems to lean closer whenever you look away.

4521.name: The Hedge Labyrinth

north.description: To the north lies The Hedge Labyrinth.

south.description: To the south lies The Hedge Labyrinth.

4521.description:
Roots as thick as ropes have lifted the gravel into ridges here, and the
hedge walls bulge where the roots have grown through them. Black berries
hang in clusters at head height, glossy and waxy. The light is a dim,
underwater green. Scraps of torn cloth flutter from the thorns, a
warning of what the hedge has taken.

4522.name: The Hedge Labyrinth

north.description: To the north lies The Hedge Labyrinth.

4522.description:
The passage opens into a wider walk, with an old stone lantern at the
corner choked by ivy. Hedge walls stand on every side, tall and dark,
and the earth underfoot is trampled hard. A glimmer of open ground shows
through a gap at the far end, where the labyrinth thins out. The silence
is thick enough to feel.

4523.name: The Dead End

west.description: To the west lies The Hedge Labyrinth.

4523.description:
The passage ends in a blank wall of ancient yew, hung with creepers that
have twisted themselves into thick, writhing curtains. The ground is
bare earth, dotted with rings of pale mushrooms. Overhead a patch of sky
shows, grey and faintly humid. The only way back is west, along the
labyrinth passage.

4524.name: In The Greenhouse

north.description: To the north lies In The Greenhouse.

east.description: To the east lies In The Greenhouse.

south.description: To the south lies Outside The Greenhouse.

west.description: To the west lies In The Greenhouse.

4524.description:
Inside the glasshouse the heat presses on you like a damp hand. Rows of
slatted benches run off into the green gloom, crowded with pots whose
tenants have long since burst their clay and rooted into the floor. The
doorway lies south, back to the garden, while the glass-roofed hall
continues north, east and west between the benches. Water drips from the
roof ribs, and every drop is tinted faintly green.

4525.name: In The Greenhouse

north.description: To the north lies In The Greenhouse.

east.description: To the east lies In The Greenhouse.

4525.description:
A workbench runs along the glass here, scarred by knives and stained
with sap in many colours. Broken seed trays and glass jars are heaped
beneath it in a tangle of dust and webs. A hand-painted sign above the
bench is blotted by mould. The aisle runs north into the corner and east
to the centre of the greenhouse.

extra_descs.sign painted mould:
Beneath the mould, a few faded letters survive: 'Doctor I. Vane,
Experimental Plantings. Do not water the specimens.'

4526.name: In The Greenhouse

east.description: To the east lies In The Greenhouse.

south.description: To the south lies In The Greenhouse.

4526.description:
This is a far corner of the glasshouse, where condensation hangs like
rain and the panes glow with green fire. Orchids dangle from the rafters
in dripping curtains, their lips red and wet and strangely toothed. A
drain in the flagstones gurgles faintly. The aisle leads east along the
rear wall and south along the side of the hall.

4527.name: In The Greenhouse

east.description: To the east lies In The Greenhouse.

south.description: To the south lies In The Greenhouse.

west.description: To the west lies In The Greenhouse.

4527.description:
This is the back of the greenhouse, where the benches give way to a bed
of black soil, churned deep. Fat pitcher plants as tall as a man nod on
thick stems, their hooded mouths brimming with a syrupy fluid that hums
with drowning flies. Narrow aisles lead east and west along the glass,
and south the way returns to the central aisle. The panes are so thick
with moisture that nothing outside can be seen.

4528.name: In The Greenhouse

south.description: To the south lies In The Greenhouse.

west.description: To the west lies In The Greenhouse.

4528.description:
In this corner of the glasshouse the iron frame is wrapped in a single
huge vine, its trunk thick as a man's waist and its leaves slick as wet
leather. Pale blossoms hang overhead, opening and closing slowly as if
they were breathing. Dead moths lie scattered on the flagstones beneath
them, dusted gold with pollen. The aisle runs south toward a door in the
side wall, and west back along the rear of the hall.

4529.name: In The Greenhouse

north.description: To the north lies In The Greenhouse.

east.description: To the east lies The Path Around The Greenhouse.

west.description: To the west lies In The Greenhouse.

4529.description:
A glass door stands in the side wall of the greenhouse, its frame wedged
open by a root as thick as a cable. Beyond it the outer path is bright
with sunlight, a welcome relief from the oppressive heat. Spiny cacti
and bloated succulents crowd the benches, bursting with swollen red
fruit. The aisle continues north into the corner and west toward the
middle of the hall, while the door leads east.

4530.name: The Rockery

north.description: To the north lies The Garden.

west.description: To the west lies The Clearing.

4530.description:
Heaps of weathered limestone have been piled into a rockery, each
crevice stuffed with alpine flowers, stonecrop and trailing moss in too-
vivid colours. Water seeps from the stones in a tiny stream that ends in
a stagnant pool, ringed with bright orange fungi. Loose rubble makes the
footing treacherous. Paths lead north to a garden of low beds and west
into a clearing.

4531.name: The Garden

north.description: To the north lies The Path Under The Trees.

south.description: To the south lies The Rockery.

west.description: To the west lies The Pavilion.

4531.description:
A garden of low box-edged beds stretches around you, the borders long
since grown shaggy and spilled together. Snapdragons gape in rows, and
bees as fat as thumbs drone drunkenly from flower to flower. Piled
stones to the south mark the rockery, the pavilion's white roof shows to
the west, and a shaded way leads north beneath old trees.

4532.name: The Path Under The Trees

east.description: To the east lies The Secret Garden.

south.description: To the south lies The Garden.

4532.description:
Old yews and crooked apple trees meet overhead, making a green tunnel
where the light falls in coins. The path underfoot is mossy and soft,
and windfalls lie rotting in the grass, split open and sticky. A faint
scent of lilies drifts from the east, where an ivy-draped archway opens
into a hidden place. South the path returns to the beds.

4533.name: The Pavilion

east.description: To the east lies The Garden.

south.description: To the south lies The Plaza.

4533.description:
An octagonal pavilion of white painted wood stands here, its roof
sagging under a mantle of climbing creeper. The floorboards are soft
with damp and strewn with petals, and lanterns hang cold from the
rafters, their glass fogged green. Tea tables are laid for guests who
never came, the cups full of rainwater and drowned blossoms. The open
sides give onto the plaza to the south and a lawn of low beds to the
east.

4534.name: The Secret Garden

west.description: To the west lies The Path Under The Trees.

4534.description:
A walled garden, secret and silent, is closed in on all sides by high
brick walls blanketed with ivy. At its heart a mad botanist's private
work lies in neat, terrible rows: flowers with human-shaped buds, and a
bed of pale bulbs that twitch in the soil. A cracked stone bench sits
beside a basin of black water. The only way out is the archway to the
west, through which the path under the trees can be seen.

extra_descs.basin black water:
The basin is cut from a single block of dark stone, and the water in it
never ripples. Stems of tiny white flowers stand up out of it, all
leaning the same way.

641400.name: spider garden giant orb-weaver
641400.long_desc: A giant garden spider hangs motionless in a web strung between two flowerbeds, its striped belly swollen.
641400.description:
The spider is as big as a hound, its legs banded yellow and black like a
wasp's. Dewdrops cling to its web and every strand quivers as it turns
to watch you.

641401.name: flytrap plant snapping man-eating
641401.long_desc: A snapping flytrap as tall as a man sways on its thick stem, its spiked jaws slowly opening.
641401.description:
Its two hinged leaves are fringed with white spines and lined in wet
crimson. Bones and scraps of cloth lie in the soil about its root.

641402.name: gardener feral man wild
641402.long_desc: A feral gardener in a tattered smock crouches among the flowers, muttering to the plants as he clips them.
641402.description:
Leaves and thorns are tangled in his beard, and his eyes shine with a
tender madness. He clutches a long, crooked blade as if it were a child.

641403.name: ogre hedge topiary living
641403.long_desc: A hulking hedge ogre, shaped of yew and bramble, stands very still among the leaves.
641403.description:
It is a giant figure of clipped hedge, with eyes of dark berries and
hands like bundles of thorned branches. Gravel rolls from its shoulders
as it breathes in the damp air.

641404.name: crocodile marsh pond huge
641404.long_desc: A huge marsh crocodile lies half submerged in the shallows, only its eyes and snout showing.
641404.description:
Its scaled back is crusted with mud and pond weed, and its jaws are
crowded with yellow teeth. It was no doubt brought here as a curiosity
and left to grow.

641405.name: queen bloom flower carnivorous plant
641405.long_desc: Queen Bloom, a vast carnivorous flower, rises from the greenhouse floor on a nest of coiling vines.
641405.description:
Her petals are crimson and cream, each as big as a door, and a sweet
drugging scent rolls off her in waves. In the dark heart of the bloom a
wet mouth gapes, ringed with thorns.

641406.name: botanist mad doctor ilmeric vane
641406.short_desc: Doctor Ilmeric Vane, the Mad Botanist
641406.long_desc: Doctor Ilmeric Vane, the Mad Botanist, bends over a bed of twitching bulbs, whispering to them.
641406.description:
He is a gaunt man in a stained green coat, his hands stained to the
wrists with sap and his hair full of petals. His eyes are bright and
fixed, and he smiles as though you were a seedling that has finally
taken root.

741400.name: sickle briar curved
741400.room_desc: A curved sickle with a briar-wood handle lies here.
741400.description: The blade is notched and stained green with old sap. The handle is a twist of living briar that still bears a few thorns.

741401.name: gloves silk spider
741401.short_desc: a pair of spider silk gloves
741401.room_desc: A pair of spider silk gloves lies here.
741401.description: The silk is pale and fine, strong enough to turn a knife yet soft against the skin.

741402.name: boots mudhide crocodile hide
741402.room_desc: A pair of boots stitched from crocodile hide lies here.
741402.description: The scaled leather is thick and waterproof, and smells faintly of the pond. The soles grip wet stone like claws.

741403.name: crown petal queen bloom
741403.room_desc: A crown of crimson petals, strangely fresh, lies here.
741403.description: The petals are as thick as leather and never wilt. Warm scent drifts from the crown, and for a moment you feel the vines listening.

741404.name: shears vane pruning silver
741404.room_desc: A pair of long silver pruning shears lies here.
741404.description: The blades are long, narrow and keen, and etched with tiny leaves. The handles are worn smooth by years of one man's hands.
